subject: Dedicated reservation options and phased ramp for MedicaSys
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Paul Hayes <paul.hayes@medicasys.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medicasys.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com, rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated reservation options and phased ramp for MedicaSys

Hi Paul —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Attached is a concise set of dedicated reservation options tailored to MedicaSys' projected inference load (based on the Q4 usage you shared). I captured three practical paths so your engineering and procurement teams can evaluate tradeoffs quickly:

1) Lean Start (3x A100-equivalent GPUs minimum) — Good for bursty proof-of-value and lower commit. Autoscale enabled up to 8 GPUs; 4 week lead time for dedicated pool build.
   - Target SLO: p95 <= 180 ms for 512-token avg workloads
   - Pricing: discounted reserved hourly + usage buffer.

2) Production Baseline (8x A100-equivalent GPUs minimum) — Predictable throughput for steady real-time features. Autoscale up to 24 GPUs; 6 week ramp to full capacity.
   - Target SLO: p95 <= 120 ms for 512-token avg workloads
   - Includes 24/7 on-call and 99.9% uptime SLA

3) Enterprise Ramp (16x A100-equivalent GPUs minimum) — For multi-service/ML pipelines and redundancy across AZs. Autoscale up to 48 GPUs; phased ramp over 3 months.
   - Target SLO: p95 <= 100 ms, multi-AZ failover
   - Includes advanced observability retention and quarterly capacity reviews

Notes and configurable knobs in the attachment: min GPUs, burst pool policy, quantization profile recommendations for cost reduction, and optional canary routing for rollout. We've also included a suggested ramp schedule keyed to your expected feature milestones (beta launch, production rollout, regulatory audit).

Next steps I recommend:
- Procurement: review the Lean Start vs Production Baseline and flag preferred commit term (monthly vs annual).
- Engineering: confirm expected concurrency and maximum sequence length for the primary inference path (we used 512 tokens as a baseline).
- I'll loop in our provisioning lead to lock lead times once you pick an option.

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min workshop this week to walk through the attachment and calibrate min-GPU sizing against your traffic shapes.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachment: MedicaSys_Dedicated_Options_v1.pdf (3 pages)
Attachment: medicasys_usage_history_Q4_2026.csv (summary)
From: Paul Hayes <paul.hayes@medicasys.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medicasys.com>, Procurement Team <procure@medicasys.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options and phased ramp for MedicaSys

Camila —

Thanks for the clear options and the deck. A few quick questions from procurement and infra:

- Can we push the minimum on the Production Baseline down to 6 GPUs for the first quarter if we commit to a 12-month term? Our forecasts have increased variance through Q2.
- What is the guaranteed provisioning lead time if we need to scale the pool by +50% mid-quarter? We need a hard SLT for procurement.
- For the Enterprise Ramp, can Redwood provide a short note on redundancy (multi-AZ vs multi-region) and any additional costs?

Also looping Lena for compliance concerns — she may ask for an audit timeline for SOC2 evidence and network segmentation details.

Can we aim to decide on option and term by Jan 25 so procurement can lock the budget?

—Paul
Director of Platform Engineering | MedicaSys
paul.hayes@medicasys.com | +1 (617) 555-0221
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Paul Hayes <paul.hayes@medicasys.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medicasys.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated reservation options and phased ramp for MedicaSys

Team — forwarding Paul's questions; quick internal notes below before I reply formally: 

(Quoted)
> Can we push the minimum on the Production Baseline down to 6 GPUs for the first quarter if we commit to a 12-month term?

Rishi — short answer: yes, but we should: 1) document the transient overcommit risk and 2) add an auto-burst layer (pay-as-you-go) to cover short-term spikes. For pricing I suggest a blended reserved rate for the first 6 GPUs + burst rate for above-min traffic. I'll ask pricing to run numbers but want your confirmation on feasibility from the runtime side.

> What is the guaranteed provisioning lead time if we need to scale the pool by +50% mid-quarter?

Vivek — what is realistic lead time for a 50% scale event in the same region assuming dedicated capacity pool exists? We should propose a firm SLT (e.g., 72 hours for software/config change + 5-7 calendar days for GPU scheduling if new hardware required). If we rely on burst shared capacity, we can make it faster but procurement will want a written fallback.

> For Enterprise Ramp, note on redundancy and costs?

We should explicitly state: multi-AZ replication (within region) is included in Enterprise Ramp; multi-region (>1 region) is available as an add-on (estimated 15% uplift to reserved pricing). 

Action items I will own: update the PDF with a Production Baseline variant (6-min / 24-max, 12-month commit pricing) and a clear SLT table for provisioning. Rishi/Vivek — can you confirm technical constraints and a recommended SLT by EOD? I want to reply to Paul with concrete commitments within the procurement timeline.

Thanks — Camila

[Quoted original attachments retained]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Paul Hayes <paul.hayes@medicasys.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medicasys.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Jan 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options and phased ramp for MedicaSys

Camila / team / Paul —

Confirmed operational constraints and proposed SLT/terms below. I'm including the updated attachment: MedicaSys_Dedicated_Options_v1 (v1.1) with the 6-GPU Production Baseline variant and a Provisioning SLT table.

Key commitments:
- Production Baseline variant: minimum 6x A100-equivalent GPUs, autoscale to 24; 12-month reserved term qualifies for blended reserved rate. We will guarantee a 72-hour software/config change window for scaling (routing, KV cache warm-up). For hardware-backed increases that require additional node scheduling, we commit to 5 business days to provision GPUs in-region (with escalation to dedicated partner pool if supply constraints arise).
- +50% scale events mid-quarter: covered by autoscale into reserved burst pool (first 24 hours) then hardware scheduling if sustained; procurement fallback: if hardware procurement needed, we reserve partner capacity to meet 5 business day provisioning for deals on 12-month terms.
- Redundancy: multi-AZ redundancy within region included for Enterprise Ramp. Multi-region is available as add-on ~15% reserved price uplift + configuration fee.
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence package and network segmentation snapshot can be delivered within 7 business days upon signed NDA.

Paul — if this aligns with MedicaSys needs, Camila can circulate v1.1 and a short contract addendum for the 12-month Production Baseline variant. If procurement wants the hard SLT incorporated into the MSA, let us know and I can work with legal to draft the clause.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: MedicaSys_Dedicated_Options_v1.1.pdf (updated pricing table and SLT)
